text.p: Liverpool completed the bargain signing of promising Norwegian defender Bjorn Tore Kvarme on a free transfer from Norwegian champions Rosenborg on Friday.
The 24-year-old utility defender has signed a three-and-a-half-year contract with the English league leaders, who beat off opposition from several top European sides including Rangers.
Kvarme, rated in the 2.0 million pounds ($3.4 million) category, was allowed to leave Rosenborg on a free transfer under the Bosman ruling.
But it is unlikely that he will make a swift debut for injury-hit Liverpool because of a delay in international clearance.
Kvarme was a childhood Liverpool fan, though he did not allow that to affect his decision in joining the club.
He said: "They had to sell the club a little bit but Liverpool is a big club and it is a big ambition for me to play for a team like this."
He has given up an opportunity to play against Italian giants Juventus in the quarter-finals of the European Cup but does not regret that decision.

He added: "I played against Milan in December and would have played against Juventus in March but that is not a problem. Sorting out my future was the priority and signing for Liverpool overshadows that."
Kvarme will effectively replace John Scales, who was recently sold to Spurs for 2.6 million pounds. Spurs also recently signed striker Steffen Iversen from Rosenborg as well.

Kvarme explained: "I played as a right back with Rosenborg but also played at centre back. They played a flat back four but Liverpool's system is different with three in the middle and I would fit on the right side of defence." ($ = 0.594 British Pounds)
